subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

By this time tomorrow / we will have / reached to Delhi.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e., **"reached to Delhi."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English grammar, certain verbs are followed directly by an object (if there is one) without a preposition; such verbs are known as “**preposition-less verbs.”** 
 
• In this case,** 'reach'** is one such verb that doesn't need a preposition ('to') after it when indicating a destination.
 
• As a general rule, the correct usage should be** 'reach + (place)' **— e.g., 'reach Delhi', 'reach the station' — and not '**reach to (place)**'.
 
• Therefore, the phrase** "reached to Delhi"** is incorrect. The correct phrasing should be** "reached Delhi."**

Therefore, the **correct answer** is - **"reached to Delhi."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is correct as it stands. "we will have" is part of a future perfect construction, which is a tense used to describe an action that will be completed before some specified point in the future.
 
• **Option 3 **is also correct. "By this time tomorrow" is a common way to reference a specific time in the future.
 
• **Option 2**, 'No error', is incorrect since there is an error in the sentence.
